<thought>
Excellent! The precipitate from the chloride test (which should be AgCl) fully dissolved in ammonia solution. This is a classic confirmatory test for Ag+ ions:

AgCl(s) + 2NH3(aq) → [Ag(NH3)2]+(aq) + Cl-(aq)

The white AgCl precipitate dissolves in ammonia to form the soluble diamminesilver(I) complex ion. This behavior is characteristic and confirmatory for silver ions.

Combined with the previous observations:
1. White precipitate with HCl (AgCl formation)
2. Brown/dark precipitate with KOH (Ag2O formation)
3. The AgCl precipitate dissolves in ammonia (forming [Ag(NH3)2]+)

All these tests confirm that the cation is Ag+ (silver ion).
</thought>
<final_answer>Ag+</final_answer>
